definition: This glossary of artificial intelligence is a list of definitions of terms and concepts relevant to the study of artificial intelligence (AI), its subdisciplines, and related fields.
details: Related glossaries include Glossary of computer science, Glossary of robotics, Glossary of machine vision, and Glossary of logic.

explainer.lead: A glossary of artificial intelligence is a shared reference for the meanings of AI terms and concepts. It helps readers, students, and practitioners discuss the same idea without talking past one another.

tiers.eli5: It is like a dictionary for the special words people use when talking about artificial intelligence. If someone says a term you do not know, you can look it up and get back to the conversation. Related glossaries do the same job for subjects such as robotics and logic.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer can use the glossary to check terminology while reading technical material, writing documentation, or discussing a project across disciplines. Its practical value is consistency: a short definition can reveal whether people are using one word for different concepts. It should not be treated as an implementation guide, and specialized work may require the related machine-learning, robotics, machine-vision, or logic literature.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is a list of definitions of terms and concepts relevant to artificial intelligence, its subdisciplines, and related fields. Its scope is terminological rather than algorithmic: it establishes reference meanings but does not itself provide proofs, experimental results, or complete technical specifications.

explainer.example: A reader encounters an unfamiliar machine-vision term while studying AI. They use the AI glossary to understand its place in the broader subject, then consult the Glossary of machine vision for more specialized vocabulary.

explainer.intuition: Think of it as a map of vocabulary: each entry connects a term to a concise explanation, making a broad and interconnected subject easier to navigate.
howItWorks: Collect terms and concepts relevant to AI, its subdisciplines, and related fields.
Pair each term with a definition of the idea it names.
Use the entries as a common reference when reading, learning, or discussing AI.
Turn to a related glossary when a term belongs more specifically to computer science, robotics, machine vision, or logic.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI spans several subdisciplines and related fields, so consistent definitions reduce ambiguity and make technical communication easier across those boundaries.
misconceptions: It is not a textbook: entries define ideas rather than teach complete methods or implementations.
It is not limited to core AI vocabulary; its scope also includes subdisciplines and related fields.
A related glossary complements it rather than replacing the entire AI glossary.
